evidence: Adult proportions with a small capsule head (P1 0.133 H), narrow waist, long legs, small foot. No chibi head, no box torso. Caveat: squared upper chest and flat shoulder tops; mannequin read.
Human proportions with a small egg-shaped head, a visible neck and a tapered torso. No chibi head and no box torso, so it does not read as a toy or character. The mannequin look is a G2/G3 problem.

Chest to waist to pelvis and thigh to shank flow, but the shoulder caps are separate tubes off a flat-topped chest block with a visible ledge; the pelvis/thigh top bulges as a kink; no deliberate dark joint recesses anywhere.
Chest, waist and pelvis, and thigh and shank, flow continuously, but there are no deliberate dark recesses at the shoulder, elbow, hip, knee or ankle; the arms hang as smooth tubes.
One uniform clay surface; a single watertight part (M1 1/1), so no geometry for dark recesses or a shell/under-structure split.
The clay render cannot show colour; geometrically there are no seams, gaps or inset zones where a dark under-structure or accent could appear.
Limbs, head and legs share soft rounding; the chest is squarer than the capsule limbs and the shoulder caps use a tighter radius; contour banding limits the judgement.
Rounded-oval sections and soft radii used consistently across head, torso, arms, legs and feet; shoulder caps slightly squarer.
At equal height the silhouette sits very close to both references (S2 IoU 0.756 / 0.775). Differs: hip/thigh flare wider, shoulders step out more abruptly, head fuller and shorter-necked.

In the equal-height lineup, head size, shoulder cap, arm length and leg length match the references (IoU 0.756 / 0.775). Differences: pelvis/thigh flare more, waist pinches more, head is a plain egg, arms angle outward.

top_changes.change: Remove the hip/thigh bulge and the abrupt shoulder ledge; round and lower the shoulder cap into a sloped shoulder line.
Create a deliberate dark under-structure read: pronounced neck/waist groove and narrow joint waists at shoulder, elbow, hip and knee.
Make the chest section rounder, in line with the limbs and head.
